{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** We built a fish facing right, and the body outline, nose and both tail fins carry from the start, so I expect the judge to read it as a fish. I laid the bottom body line (stroke 2) and the bottom tail edge, which was about a third of the visible shape. The result isn't clean. By my last look, the start would knock over about 131 of the 189 standing dominoes, so roughly 58 are loose and won't fall. Some of those are pale strays on the right side of the tail. I also said I'd lift the stray line inside the body near the top-left, and it still looks to be standing there. It's invisible if it doesn't fall, but I didn't finish what I said I'd do.

**Execution:** I started the bottom run promptly, kept clear of Leo's top line, and checked the joints. The tail's bottom corner was the weak spot. My first quick fix didn't take, so I laid a proper join and finished it at 9:45, then went hands off before the push. I didn't verify the corner with a close inspection at the end, so I can't promise it holds. I should have inspected the strays earlier instead of leaving them for the end.

**Collaboration:** I kept roles clear. I took the bottom tail edge so Maya could keep the top, and I told Leo when his bottom fin wasn't needed because mine was already standing. I said clearly when I was working near the corner and asked others to keep clear, so we avoided bumps. I stayed hands off in the last minutes, as the group agreed.

**Leadership:** Leo set the plan and Priya's sketch gave us the shape, so I mostly followed. I stepped up when the bottom run was short and when the corner needed fixing, and I flagged the stray early. I could have pushed harder on cleaning up loose dominoes while there was time."}
